newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, helped by XAU index.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, helped by XAU index.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher Wednesday for the fifth straight session, helped by sharp gains in mining stocks in Philadelphia Stock Exchange's gold and silver sector stock index and related options.

"We saw more fund shortcovering and rolling forward into April and December gold futures, but I don't think you can ignore the move in the mining stocks either, which have been looking undervalued by comparison with the rest of the stockmarket," Linnco Futures Group's Chicago trader Anthony Raia said.

COMEX December gold closed up $0.80 at $384.20 an ounce after setting a 10-day session high at $385.80, not far from resistance around $386.00, set by the highs in late October. Total gold futures volume was a high 65,000 lots.
"We didn't get through resistance today, with trade and producer selling seen on the first attempt as expected, but I think December gold could get back up to $395," Raia said.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted around $383.05/45, down from the London afternoon fix of $383.60 but up from the New York close Tuesday around $382.20/70.
Gold prices are recovering from an 18-months low of $376.80 plumbed Nov 1 after a long decline from a five-year high of $417.70 set February.
Philadelphia Stock Exchange's gold and silver sector index (.XAU) was up 1.18 points near the close at 127.25, after seeing a 10-week high intraday at 129.63.
The index is recovering from a 12-month low of 113.44 established Nov 6.
The move up in gold equities reflects investors views that gold stocks are cheap relative to other stocks and that gold itself may now be relatively cheap, analysts said.
The spot gold/silver ratio ended little changed around 78.18, though most activity was seen Wednesday in the gold market, traders said.
COMEX December silver ended up 1.8 cents at $4.900, off a session peak of $4.940. Resistance was seen initially around $4.950 and then $5.000, traders said.
With both the December gold and silver contracts due to enter the delivery period Nov 27, more shortcovering could push prices up further, analysts said.
COMEX December gold open interest fell 6,155 lots to 84,198 lots Tuesday, while total open interest in gold futures fell 5,727 lots, as funds covered short positions.
December gold open interest currently represents around 8.4 million ounces, while available warehouse stocks are only about 1.06 million ounces, analysts noted.
December silver open interest was around 285 million ounces, but total warehouse stocks only amount to about 135 million ounces.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $0.40 at $391.60, with NYMEX December palladium up $3.65 at $123.50, its highest since mid-September.

Tuesday, Johnson Matthey, the world's largest refiner of platinum group metals, forecast the supply of palladium would move into a deficit this year of 130,000 ounces from a surplus last year of 240,000 ounces.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1640; email: clive.mckeef@reuter.com
